subject: Penetration test report & evidence request — redaction, embargo, and access proposal
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@acmesoft.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: full penetration test report + raw evidence (NDA attached)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Our security team needs to review Redwood's latest internal penetration test (performed June 2027) for our procurement checklist (SIG/SOC2 evidence). Can you provide: 1) the full pen test report, 2) raw evidence attachments (screenshots, payload logs) used by the tester, and 3) an executive summary that our InfoSec reviewers can distribute internally?

We are happy to sign a mutual NDA. I've attached AcmeSoft's standard mutual NDA to this thread — please let me know if you'd prefer to use Redwood's. The timeline is tight: our procurement window closes on Aug 20 and we'd like to complete the security evaluation by Aug 17.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Security Program Manager, AcmeSoft
(attachment: Acme_Redwood_Mutual_NDA_Draft_20270809.pdf (PDF))
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report + raw evidence (NDA attached)

Alice — appreciate the clear ask and the NDA. Looping in Monica (security engineering) and Jonas (legal) to confirm what we can share and under what controls. High level: we can share the full report and exec summary under a mutual NDA, but raw evidence (screenshots/payloads) requires additional redaction and a short embargo/controlled-access approach for tester privacy and customer data minimization.

Proposed next steps: 
- Monica to propose a redaction matrix and timeline (we can likely deliver a redacted full report + exec summary in 3 business days after NDA).
- If Acme needs unredacted evidence, we can provide it in a secure data room (watermarked, time-limited S3 access) after a documented access request + narrow scope approval; we typically require a 30-day embargo on distribution for tester privacy and to allow remediation.
- Jonas to review Acme NDA and propose any carrier changes (we prefer mutual with limited liability carveouts).

Will treat this as high priority to meet your Aug 17 window if we lock in the NDA this week. Monica — can you pick this up and outline redaction rules and an initial list of categories we will redact?

—Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report + raw evidence (NDA attached)

Thanks Rishi — I can own the redaction plan. Quick notes and constraints from the security team: 

Redaction principles we propose:
- Remove any customer-identifying URIs, hostnames, and IPs unless they are necessary to reproduce an issue; replace with pseudonyms (e.g., <HOST-123>) and an anonymized mapping table.
- Strip any PII from screenshots and logs (usernames, emails, tokens).
- Aggregate or obfuscate payloads that contain customer query material; provide sanitized payloads that preserve the attack vector but not the original content.
- Preserve technical detail of vulnerability root cause, affected components, exploitation steps, and remediation guidance.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Day 1 (by EOD Aug 10): deliver redaction_proposal_matrix_20270810.xlsx (attached) describing categories and examples.
- Day 2 (Aug 11): produce a redacted full report + exec summary (PDF) and a redaction log (summary of what was removed).
- If Acme requests raw, unredacted evidence: prepare a controlled access data room with time-limited signed URLs, watermarking, and mandatory non-disclosure for all viewers. We recommend the embargo period of 30 days from access, during which distribution is prohibited.

Questions for Acme (please respond in-thread):
1) Do you require the original tester's raw payloads (full logs) or will sanitized payloads that show reproduction steps suffice for your SIG review?
2) Who at Acme will need access (list names/emails) if we prepare the secure data room?

I'll attach the matrix now.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redaction_proposal_matrix_20270810.xlsx (XLSX))
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmesoft.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@acmesoft.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report + raw evidence (NDA attached)

Rishi / Monica — thanks for the fast turnaround and the matrix. A few clarifications: 

- For SIG and our internal risk committee we do prefer the raw tester payloads and screenshots where they show proof of concept; sanitized payloads are sometimes insufficient for our auditors.
- Access list: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmesoft.com>, Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@acmesoft.com>, and Priya Kumar <p.kumar@acmesoft.com> (Application Security Lead).
- Regarding embargo: Acme is comfortable with a 14-day limited embargo rather than 30 days. We will not distribute externally and will log all downloads.

If Redwood can provide the full unredacted evidence inside a secure, watermarked data room with per-user access logs and a 14-day embargo, we can accept that. We can sign Redwood's mutual NDA if you prefer (please send).

Goal: receive secure access to evidence by Aug 13 to meet our internal schedule.

Thanks,
Alice
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmesoft.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report + raw evidence (NDA attached)

Alice,

Appreciate the clear answers. Two quick legal/controls items from our side: 
1) NDA: I've attached a short mutual NDA template we prefer for red-team/evidence exchange (I sent via DocuSign link below). It limits liability and includes a narrow permitted use clause for security reviews only. If Acme redlines material provisions, please flag them quickly so we can escalate.
2) Access controls: Redwood will grant per-user S3 access to a secure evidence bucket with object-level watermarking and access logs. We require: acknowledgement of the embargo period in the DocuSign agreement, a list of named viewers (you provided three — please confirm Priya's full name), and acceptance that the evidence will not be redistributed outside Acme without prior written consent during the embargo. After embargo ends, Acme may retain copies for internal audit purposes only.

Proposed compromise on embargo: 14-day embargo for download/distribution + a 30-day notification window where Acme will notify Redwood before any external distribution (we expect external distribution to be rare and to require written approval).

If that works, Rishi will send the DocuSign NDA and Monica will provision the secure data room with the three named users. Target: DocuSign out today, data room access by EOD Aug 12.

Jonas Weber
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
(related link: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Agreement-Token)
